content.value_statement: Layered Go configuration can fail through incorrect precedence, binding, or decoding. This skill provides focused Viper patterns for reliable setup, testing, and reloads.
actual_capabilities: Explains Viper precedence across explicit values, flags, environment variables, files, remote stores, and defaults.
Guides environment binding with prefixes, key replacers, exact variable names, and empty-value handling.
Shows config file discovery, merging, embedded defaults, supported formats, and optional-file error handling.
Covers struct decoding with mapstructure tags, subtrees, decode hooks, and unknown-key collection.
Provides isolated testing and synchronized hot-reload patterns for Go services.
limitations: It does not replace the official Viper API documentation or verify behavior for every library version.
It does not manage secrets, provision remote stores, or configure production access controls.
It does not provide complete Cobra command architecture beyond Viper flag binding.
Hot-reload examples require adaptation to each application's validation and concurrency model.

use_cases.title: Configure a Go Service
use_cases.description: Create layered file and environment configuration with predictable precedence and optional config files.

use_cases.title: Connect Cobra Flags
use_cases.description: Bind CLI flags before execution so explicit values override environment variables and files correctly.

use_cases.title: Harden Runtime Reloads
use_cases.description: Validate candidate settings and synchronize updates before replacing active service configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Viper for my Go service using a YAML file, MYAPP-prefixed environment variables, and sensible defaults.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new service

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Environment Binding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why MYAPP_DATABASE_HOST does not override database.host, then provide the correct Viper prefix, replacer, and AutomaticEnv setup.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Configuration Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my Viper tests to avoid shared global state. Use isolated instances and temporary environment values.

prompt_templates.title: Design Safe Hot Reload
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Viper reload flow that debounces events, decodes a candidate, validates it, and atomically updates synchronized application state.

output_examples.input: Why does an environment variable for database.host remain ignored?
output_examples.output: The diagnosis identifies the missing dot-to-underscore key replacer and lists the required prefix, replacer, and automatic binding sequence.

output_examples.input: How should an optional configuration file be loaded?
output_examples.output: The response distinguishes a missing file from parsing or permission errors, allowing only the missing-file case to continue.

output_examples.input: How can a service reload configuration without data races?
output_examples.output: The response proposes candidate decoding, validation, synchronized replacement, error logging, and retention of the previous valid configuration.

best_practices: Configure the environment prefix and key replacer before enabling automatic environment lookup.
Use explicit mapstructure tags and validate decoded configuration before application startup or reload.
Create a separate Viper instance for each test and protect shared runtime configuration with synchronization.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on the global Viper instance across tests because state persists between cases.
Do not ignore every ReadInConfig error because malformed or unreadable files require attention.
Do not update shared configuration directly from a watch callback without validation and synchronization.

faq.question: Can Viper be used without Cobra?
faq.answer: Yes. Services can use Viper for files and environment variables without adding a command framework.

faq.question: Which configuration source has highest priority?
faq.answer: Explicit Set values lead, followed by flags, environment variables, files, remote stores, and defaults.

faq.question: Why do nested environment keys fail?
faq.answer: Viper preserves dots unless a key replacer maps them to underscores before environment lookup.

faq.question: How should optional config files be handled?
faq.answer: Continue only for ConfigFileNotFoundError. Return parsing, permission, and other real errors.

faq.question: How can tests avoid Viper state leakage?
faq.answer: Create a new Viper instance per test and use the test framework's temporary environment support.

faq.question: Does this skill access credentials or remote services?
faq.answer: No. It documents binding and remote-provider patterns, but it does not read credentials or initiate connections.
